To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the invariant cross-section of 5 Gev/c π± and K± secondaries produced at centre-of-mass energy 53 GeV, is approximately the same as that at 19GeV centre-of-mass-energy for the same value of Feynman variable (x) in the region 0.15<pT<0.95GeV/c, where pT is the transverse momentum of the secondary.

(i) at 19 Gev/c, the invariant cross-section for pions and kaons is a function of x and pT; and (ii) at 53 Gev/c, invariant cross-sections for pions and protons are a function of x, pT and the Feynman x variable.
the transverse momentum distribution of 5 Gev/c pions and Kaons produced at 53GeV in the centre of the mass is approximately the same as that at 19GeV accelerator energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the transverse momentum distribution of secondaries produced at the ISR.
the study of the production of secondaries in proton proton collisions at the CERN Intersecting Storage Rings.
the transverse momentum distributions of secondaries produced in the central region of proton-proton collisions.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transverse momentum distribution of the 5 GeV/ c secondaries is approximately the same at 53 Gev as at 19 Gev.
the invariant cross-sections of the secondaries produced in proton-proton collisions at 53 and 19 GeV in the range 1 < x < 0.15 are approximately the same for all particles studied.
the transverse momentum dependence of the invariant π± and K± cross-section is approximately the same for 19 and 53 GeV accelerator energy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that the 5 GeV / c secondaries produced by 53 GeV protons in the CERN ISR are not produced in the same way as the 5 GeVs / c secondaries at the 19 GeV ISR.
, for p and K+, a significant difference is seen at pT > 0.95, with the cross-sections at 53 Gev being about 30% lower than at 19 Gev.
